newsitem.title: BELGIUM: KRAFT JACOBS SUCHARD NOT TO USE GENE SOYA FOR NOW.
newsitem.headline: KRAFT JACOBS SUCHARD NOT TO USE GENE SOYA FOR NOW.

text.p: Leading chocolate company Kraft Jacobs Suchard SA said on Friday it would not use controversial genetically modified soybeans in its European products for now, but was not opposed to the bean in principle on safety grounds.

"In a number of countries we found the regulatory situation regarding modified soya and foodstuffs was uncertain. We decided therefore that any products that contain soya or derivatives will for now be sourced from normally grown soya," Cynthia von Maerestetten, KJS's director of European affairs told Reuters.
She denied the company's action was linked to fears over genetically modified soya by environmental group Greenpeace.

Greenpeace held up the first shipments of the U.S.-made soya to Hamburg and Antwerp on the grounds genetically modified organisms might be able to reproduce and mutate creating organisms which could do irreversible damage to the environment.
Von Maerestetten said, however, that KJS had no doubts over the safety of the soya.

"On the contrary, we think the modified soya and ingredients from it do not pose a problem. Certainly all the scientific and regulatory authorities who have looked at it have concluded the same thing," she said.
She declined to comment on where KJS sourced its soya or name the countries where KJS believed there remain doubts over the legal framework governing genetically modified soya.
